unmappedTarget.reason: Complete printed TR adds tōn kymatōn of-the-waves after violence. Exact N1904 ends with violence and has no independent waves noun/possessor phrase at this point; no previous sea/wind occurrence is borrowed.

27:42.sourceText: Τῶν δὲ στρατιωτῶν βουλὴ ἐγένετο ἵνα τοὺς δεσμώτας ἀποκτείνωσιν, μή τις ἐκκολυμβήσας διαφύγῃ·
27:42.targetText: And the soldiers’ counsel was that they should kill the prisoners, lest anyone having swam out should escape,

groups.note: Actual stratiōtōn is genitive-plural soldiers noun, rendered English possessive soldiers’ with its real genitive and nominal head retained.
Actual egeneto is second-aorist nonactive/deponent becoming/happening predicate, rendered was in the counsel/content frame rather than a source eimi substitution.
Actual apokteinōsin is aorist active third-plural subjunctive, expanded they-should-kill with its actual mood retained.
Actual ekkolymbēsas is one aorist active nominative-singular swimming-out compound, rendered exact LSV having-swam-out with no separate Greek out word or repair of the displayed English form.

Actual diaphygē is second-aorist active third-singular subjunctive V-2AAS-3S, rendered should-escape. Complete printed TR has diaphygoi optative spelling, while the actual N1904 subjunctive form remains.

27:43.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης βουλόμενος διασῶσαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐκώλυσεν αὐτοὺς τοῦ βουλήματος, ἐκέλευσέν τε τοὺς δυναμένους κολυμβᾶν ἀπορίψαντας πρώτους ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξιέναι,
27:43.targetText: but the centurion, resolving to save Paul, hindered them from the counsel, and commanded those able to swim, having cast themselves out first—to get to the land,

groups.note: Actual boulomenos is present nonactive/deponent nominative-singular willing/intending participle, rendered resolving with its real boulomai head.
Actual diasōsai is aorist active saving-through/safe-preserving infinitive, rendered to-save while retaining its actual diasōzō compound.
Actual genitive article/counsel jointly supplies from-the-counsel as the hindering complement, retaining its nominal case/head without an independently printed from preposition.
Actual accusative-plural article nominalizes the ability participle as those, retaining its actual article identity rather than an invented demonstrative.
Actual dynamenous is present nonactive/deponent accusative-plural ability participle, rendered able without retagging it as a source adjective.

Actual aporipsantas is an aorist active accusative-plural throwing-off/out participle with the swimmers. In this intransitive nautical use it is expanded having-cast-themselves-out; no independently printed Greek reflexive pronoun is claimed, and the actual active form remains.
Actual prōtous is accusative-masculine-plural first superlative adjective A-APM-S used of those entering first, rendered first without a source adverb retag.
Actual exienai is present active going-out infinitive of exeimi, rendered to-get in the land-destination frame; no separate source obtaining verb is substituted.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article with Paul is not separately expressed in English.

27:44.sourceText: καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς οὓς μὲν ἐπὶ σανίσιν, οὓς δὲ ἐπί τινων τῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου. καὶ οὕτως ἐγένετο πάντας διασωθῆναι ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.
27:44.targetText: and the rest, some indeed on boards, and some on certain things of the ship; and thus it came to pass that all came safe to the land.

groups.note: Actual loipous is accusative-plural remaining adjective used personally, rendered rest without a separately printed remaining-people noun.
Actual hous relative is used as the first member of the some/others distribution, rendered some; the second actual relative owns the separate second some without invented tis source pronouns.
Actual tinōn is genitive-neuter-plural indefinite pronoun/adjective X-GPN, rendered certain with its real case retained.
Actual genitive-neuter-plural article nominalizes the from-the-ship material phrase, rendered things without an independently printed things noun.
Actual apo source/origin preposition is rendered of in the ship-material phrase, retaining apo rather than a source genitive-only relation inferred from English.

Actual egeneto is second-aorist nonactive/deponent happening predicate, expanded it-came-to-pass-that as English expresses the infinitival result in a finite clause. No independent Greek it pronoun, pass noun or hoti that is printed.
Actual pantas is accusative-plural all adjective used personally as subject of the safe-preserving infinitive, rendered all while its real accusative remains.

Actual diasōthēnai is aorist passive saving-through/safe-preserving infinitive, rendered finite came-safe in the result clause. Its actual passive infinitive and diasōzō head remain, not a source came verb or safe adjective.
Actual epi destination preposition supplies to in the land-arrival phrase, not a substituted eis source head.
